tools.name: score_ip
tools.description: Risk-score an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Detects commercial VPNs (naming the provider where its own published list confirms it), proxies, Tor exit nodes and datacenter hosting, and returns geolocation, ASN and a 0-100 risk score with an allow/review/block verdict.

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Check an email for syntax, MX records, disposable/throwaway providers, role accounts (info@, admin@), homograph lookalikes and domain age. Returns a 0-100 risk score and an allow/review/block verdict.

tools.name: lookup_phone
tools.description: Validate a phone number worldwide against its national numbering plan. Returns E.164, country, line type (mobile/fixed/VoIP/toll-free/premium) and a risk score. Works globally, not US-only.

tools.name: score_domain
tools.description: Profile a domain: registration date from RDAP, registrar, MX/SPF/DMARC configuration, disposable-mail and risky-TLD detection. newly_registered is null when the age genuinely could not be determined — treat that as unknown, not as 'established'.

tools.name: score_device
tools.description: Judge a browser fingerprint from /fp.js: headless detection, automation frameworks (Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright), timezone-versus-IP mismatch and repeat-device history. Note the ceiling honestly — the declared signals it relies on are the first thing stealth tooling patches, so a clean result is

tools.name: verify_agent
tools.description: Cryptographically verify a Web Bot Auth signature (RFC 9421) — proof of WHICH agent is calling, not a guess from the user-agent. Returns verified true/false plus the agent's identity and declared purpose. This is the only check here that proves rather than infers, so it carries no score and no verdi

tools.name: score_user
tools.description: Score an entire signup in one call — any combination of IP, email, phone and domain — returning a single weighted risk score, a verdict, and the top contributing signals. A hard block on any component is never averaged away. This is the tool to use when judging a person rather than a value.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: score_ip, verify_email · Private data: verify_email · Public sink: verify_email, score_user.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: score_ip, verify_email · Private data: verify_email · Public sink: verify_email, score_user

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
